apropos.p1: DEVIA started from a simple observation: timber frame companies are buried under small quotes that rarely turn into work.
apropos.p2Apres: on average to price, are never billed, and eat time that could go to more serious projects.
apropos.p3: DEVIA also answers the price and the complexity of existing software, built for design offices rather than for the tradespeople doing the work day to day.
apropos.p4: Our mission is to put proper digital tools within reach of timber frame professionals. Whether you work alone or run a team of five, you deserve something powerful, obvious to use, and fairly priced.
apropos.p5: DEVIA brings together modern artificial intelligence and a close knowledge of French building standards (the Eurocodes). The result: professional quotes in seconds, with a clear 3D view to show your customers.
apropos.v1: Software should be obvious to use.
apropos.v2: Calculations based on the official standards, so your quotes hold up.
apropos.v3: Your company data stays with you. Nothing is shared with outside AI.
apropos.v4: Turning hours into minutes, so you can get back to the jobs that matter.
apropos.projet: DEVIA is French software, built by a team that cares about timber and about code. We work alongside professional carpenters so the software follows what actually happens on site.

actualite.intro: New features, calculation improvements, 3D upgrades: follow everything that changes in the software right here.
actualite.finalTexte: DEVIA is developed continuously alongside professional carpenters.
actualite.n0T: A quote PDF worthy of an engineering file
actualite.n0X: Project perspective and design loads in the header, prices broken down by category with the detail of every member, full-page 3D views following the quote. Timber quantities are now driven by the 3D engine's own take-off.
actualite.n1X: Close to a hundred structural references (cross-laminated, glulam, KVH, framing, LVL) with their commercial lengths. A purlin runs in a single piece up to 13 m in cross-laminated timber, and the quote names the exact reference.
actualite.n2T: Valleys: grafting roofs the way the site does it
actualite.n2X: A lower wing cuts into the slope of the main body: valleys bearing on the load-carrying structure, ridge continued into the slope, jack rafters, roofing trimmed along the valleys. Trade practice, not an approximation.
actualite.n3T: Roof overhangs across the whole chain
actualite.n3X: Read off the drawing by the analysis, editable in the manual breakdown, rendered in 3D: extended rafters, purlin tails, verge rafters. The roof outline is never mistaken for the walls again.
actualite.n4T: IFC export: the real assembly, member by member
actualite.n4X: The IFC file carries the project's complete assembly: every member leaves with its exact position, orientation and section, ready for your design software.
actualite.n5X: King posts, struts and balcony brackets are now sized in compression with a buckling check to Eurocode 5, based on the official tables.
actualite.n6T: Solar panels on sheds and monopitch roofs
actualite.n6X: Photovoltaic layout reaches agricultural and monopitch roofs: compliant setting-out with safety margins, and the structural load fed straight into the section calculation.
actualite.n7X: Quote, 3D view and verification table now show exactly the same sections, mountain regional sections included. One single truth, from the form to the PDF.
actualite.n8X: Purlins set plumb on their cleats, mitred cuts at the ridge, ridge braces: shed structures reach the level of detail of traditional roof carpentry.
actualite.n9X: Cantilevered balconies get their three-piece brackets, sized to the regulatory load for residential balconies and anchored on the real face of the walls.

guides.g0E2D: Roofing, timber species, finish: the appearance you want for the structure.
guides.g0E3D: Give the town: wind, snow, seismic data and altitude update on their own.
guides.g0E4D: Choose which material prices to use - yours or DEVIA's - and start the generation.
guides.g1T: A complete quote from a PDF drawing or a photo
guides.g1I: DEVIA has three ways of creating a project: the form for simple quotes, multi-structure for bigger projects with no unusual geometry, and importing PDF drawings or photos. This last mode reads the drawings of a new build, extracts the fabrication data, pre-fills the form and keeps the geometry of the structures. An automated process that asks only one action of you.
guides.g1E0D: In the form, click the add-files button and import your PDF drawing or your photo.
guides.g1E1D: DEVIA reads the file: dimensions, heights, pitch, town and the breakdown of volumes are extracted and pre-filled.
guides.g1E2D: Review what has been read, adjust if needed, then generate: the quote and the 3D model follow the geometry of the drawing.
guides.g2T: Several structures in a single quote
guides.g2I: The standard form mode creates one structure. By choosing Custom structure in the Type of structure field, you stack several structures into one 3D view and one quote: DEVIA works out where each added structure goes and how it is arranged around the base structure, following building practice.
guides.g2E0D: In the form, Type of structure field: select Custom structure to switch to multi-structure mode.
guides.g2E1D: Describe the base structure, then add the others - house, garage, porch, balcony - each with its own dimensions.
guides.g2E2D: Each structure is calculated on its own, then positioned and arranged around the base structure. One 3D view, one quote.
guides.g3T: Bring your own catalogue to your projects
guides.g3I: DEVIA ships with a price catalogue based on a market average and updated regularly: by default your projects are priced on DEVIA's market rates. Once you bring in your own materials and prices, those apply to your projects - and the DEVIA market fills in whatever your catalogue is missing.
guides.g3E0D: Catalogue page: add your materials with their description, their unit and your price.
guides.g3E1D: When generating, select My catalogue: your prices take priority in the pricing.
guides.g3E2T: Let the market fill the gaps
guides.g3E2D: For materials missing from your catalogue, DEVIA completes automatically with market prices.
guides.g4I: DEVIA offers professionals - carpenters and design offices alike - two kinds of section calculated under Eurocode 5. MINIMUM sections are the smallest sections required for a member to carry the structure: the strict result of the calculation. RECOMMENDED sections answer to trade practice and to what the region expects visually.
guides.g4E0D: After generation, the Calculation tab shows permanent loads, snow, wind and the Eurocode 5 checks for your town.
guides.g4E1D: The smallest section the calculation requires for each member of the structure.
guides.g4E2D: The section used in trade and regional practice, shown by default - a button switches the 3D view between minimum and recommended.
guides.g5T: Give your work its full value
guides.g5I: DEVIA's strength is to carry you from A to Z through your project. Once the quote is finished, export the PDF to present it to the client. If the job goes ahead, DEVIA exports the 3D structure to your usual design software through the IFC export - so you can carry on where DEVIA stops.
guides.g5E0T: Export the quote as a PDF
guides.g5E0D: Logo, contact details, priced items and 3D views: the document is ready to put in front of the client.
guides.g5E1D: The quote becomes a job: the structure calculated in DEVIA is the basis for everything that follows.
guides.g5E2D: Export IFC button on the 3D view: every member leaves with its position, its orientation and its section, ready for your design software.
